Russia-Ukraine War Cruise Missile Hits Poland Amid Russian Strikes on Ukraine Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk announced that a team had been established to determine what the object was and personally visited the crash site. Save Mark Us Preferred on Google Print Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk in London on May 27, 2026. Jack Taylor/Reuters Guy Birchall 7/30/2026 | Updated: 7/30/2026 0:00 X 1 Poland was hit by a cruise missile during a heavy bout of Russian airstrikes on Ukraine, NATO and the Polish government stated on July 30. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said in a post on X that a Kh-101 cruise missile “violated the Polish airspace and fell 50 km away from the town of Lublin,” noting that the missile was armed. NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte said in a post on X that he had spoken with Tusk about the “violation of Poland’s airspace by a Russian missile.” “This incident is yet another reckless act by Russia and a dangerous consequence of its war against Ukraine,” Rutte said, before reaffirming the alliance’s “unwavering” commitment to supporting Kyiv. In the early hours of July 30, Warsaw scrambled fighter jets to secure its airspace amid Moscow’s aerial bombardment of its neighbor, which killed at least eight people in neighboring Ukraine, including one in Kyiv, in attacks that stretched as far as the western city of Lviv, more than 40 miles from the Polish border. “During nighttime hours, national and allied reconnaissance systems detected intense combat activity by the Russian Federation’s long-range aviation,” the Polish Operational Command of the Armed Forces stated in a July 30 post on X. Related Stories Poland Unveils First Long-Range Drone to Boost Strike Capability UK, Poland, Netherlands, Finland Make Progress on Defense Spending Plan “To ensure the safety of Polish airspace, the combat readiness of air defense system assets was elevated, including pairs of on-duty fighters and an early warning aircraft. ... At 3:40 a.m., an unidentified object moving westward was detected in Polish airspace.” Polish Operational Command said that an on-duty F-16 was then dispatched to the area to “identify and intercept” the object, but before it could be identified, “the object disappeared from radar system indications” at 3:46 a.m. Subsequently, a helicopter was sent to the last known location of the object and located “the probable crash site of the object in an undeveloped area near the village of Tarnawa-Kolonia in the Lublin Voivodeship.” “A Ground Search and Rescue Team and the relevant services were dispatched to the scene. Operational and securing actions are ongoing at the incident site,” Polish Operational Command stated. “An unidentified object moving westward was detected in Polish airspace,” the operational command of the armed forces said on X, noting that it disappeared from radars soon after the sighting at 3:40 a.m. The crater was about 10 meters wide, Polish Interior Ministry spokesperson Karolina Gałecka said on X, noting that it was found just more than a mile away from some buildings. Police in the Lublin area stated in a post on X that they received reports of a “powerful explosion” in Biłgoraj county, between the villages of Tarnawa Kolonia and Biskupice. “Officers discovered a crater and scattered debris from an unidentified object in a field located about 2 km (1.2 miles) from the nearest buildings, between the villages,” the police stated, noting that they had secured the area. Following the discovery, Tusk said he had established a special coordination team to investigate the incident and later posted a photograph of himself at the crash site. “All the indications are that it was a Russian Kh-101 ballistic missile, but we want to be 100 percent certain about the type of missile and who launched it,” Tusk told an emergency meeting. “There was no direct threat because the missile landed in an uninhabited area; we were ready to shoot it down had it continued its flight.” Tusk’s view was backed up by an X post from Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha, who said that “overnight, a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile crossed into Poland as part of Russia’s massive strike against Ukraine, violating NATO airspace.” “This is yet another clear demonstration that strengthening Ukraine’s air defense now is urgent and serves as a guarantee for the protection of the entire Euro-Atlantic community,” Sybiha said, noting in a later post on X that he had spoken with Polish Foreign Minister Radek Sikorski. Moscow has not yet commented on the incident in Poland, but the Russian Defense Ministry confirmed in a July 30 post on Telegram that it had “launched a massive strike using long-range air, land, and sea-based precision weapons, as well as attack drones, against military industrial facilities, telecommunications and logistics centers” across a range of cities in Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said in a July 30 post on X that “Kyiv and the region, as well as our Dnipro, Lviv, Poltava, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv, Sumy, Vinnytsia, Cherkasy, and Ivano-Frankivsk regions, came under attack overnight.” “Dozens of ordinary homes, civilian businesses, and infrastructure facilities were destroyed and damaged. More than 70 missiles were used in this strike, a significant number of them ballistic. There were also over 280 attack drones,” he said, noting that Ukrainian air defenses had managed to down the majority of the drones and a “significant number of cruise missiles.” In 2022, just a few months into Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, a Ukrainian missile struck a Polish village and killed two people. The incident sparked speculation that Russia had fired the missile into Polish territory. Shortly after the missile struck Polish territory, the Polish Foreign Ministry issued a statement claiming the projectile was of Russian manufacture. Soon afterward, U.S. President Joe Biden declared that “preliminary information” appeared to indicate that Russia had not fired the missile. U.S. military officials agreed, citing “initial findings” suggesting that Ukrainian air defenses had fired the missile to intercept Russian missiles. In September 2025, Poland’s Armed Forces Operational Command stated that air traffic restrictions had been introduced along the country’s eastern border with Belarus and Ukraine, following the downing of suspected Russian drones in the NATO member’s airspace. Polish authorities said at the time that a home in the village of Wyryki-Wola had likely been hit by a Russian drone that entered Poland’s airspace on the night of Sept. 9. Polish Minister for Special Services Tomasz Siemoniak told Polish television later that month that the house was likely hit by a missile fired from a Polish F-16 fighter jet. “Everything indicates that it was a missile fired by our plane, defending Poland, defending the fatherland, defending our citizens,” Siemoniak said at the time. Reuters contributed to this report. https://www.politico.eu/article/marine-l.text: PARIS — Far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen still wants to take France out of NATO’s integrated command — but won’t do so while Russia's war in Ukraine still rages on. "As long as there is a war on Europe's doorstep, this is not the time to take action in that regard, but of course my will to do so remains," the National Rally leader told POLITICO on Thursday at the Playbook Paris Live summit . Le Pen is the front-runner in next spring’s high-stakes presidential election to replace Emmanuel Macron, according to polls. Advertisement Advertisement She and far-left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon both want Paris to leave the military alliance, raising alarm bells at NATO headquarters about France's future defense policy. The National Rally has long advocated withdrawing from NATO's integrated command, but Le Pen's comments indicate a slight shift in her position. Back in May, she said France would pull out during her first term, without referring to the war in Ukraine, while the party's president Jordan Bardella wanted to wait for a peace agreement between Kyiv and Moscow. Le Pen and Bardella are campaigning as a ticket that would see the 31-year-old become prime minister. Le Pen also said that France should not enter into a war with Russia, a nuclear-armed power, and rejected the notion that it is currently in a conflict with Moscow despite the Kremlin's hybrid attacks against European nations. By publishing a statement condemning Russia last week, Le Pen and Bardella sought to fend off attacks from center-right and center-left opponents who have frequently portrayed the party as an ally to Russian President Vladimir Putin. However, Le Pen repeated her pledge Thursday to stop financial help to Ukraine if she wins next year's presidential election. Advertisement Advertisement “We can train their soldiers and their military leadership, and provide them with military aid. We can no longer provide financial assistance to Ukraine, and we regret that,” she said. However, she did not push back against the Coalition of the Willing, a group led by France and the U.K. that aims to provide a military presence in Ukraine once the war ends. "A potential peacekeeping force that’s actually quite similar to UN peacekeepers seems entirely feasible to me. And if the Coalition of the Willing is one of the conditions for negotiating a ceasefire, then I would obviously be in favor of moving forward with this proposal," she told POLITICO.
